chunks: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the married person when he flees from the pit — will he be returned until the prescribed penalty (hadd) is carried out upon him?' He said: 'He will be returned and not returned.' I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'If he was the one who confessed against himself, then fled from the pit after some stones had hit him, he will not be returned. But if only the proof (bayyina) was established against him while he was denying it, then he fled, he shall be returned humiliated until the prescribed penalty is carried out against him.

And that is because Ma'iz ibn Malik confessed before the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) to having committed adultery (zina), so he ordered that he be stoned. He fled from the pit. Al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam struck him with a camel's leg, tripping him so that he fell. The people caught up with him and killed him. Then they informed the Messenger of God of that, and he said to them: 'Why did you not leave him alone when he fled, to go away? For he was only the one who had confessed against himself.' And he said to them: 'Had Ali been present with you, you would not have gone astray.'
He (the Imam) said: And the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) paid his blood money (diya) from the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Al-Diya: blood money or compensation paid to the family of someone killed; here paid by the Prophet from the public treasury as an acknowledgment that Ma'iz should not have been killed
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَة: Al-Bayyina: evidentiary proof established by witnesses, as distinct from self-confession (iqrar)
key_terms.الْحَدّ: Al-Hadd: the prescribed legal penalty fixed by Islamic law for specific major offences
key_terms.الْحَفِيرَة: Al-Hafira: the pit dug in the ground into which the condemned is placed before stoning
key_terms.الْمُحْصَن: Muhsan: a married person who is subject to the hadd penalty of stoning (rajm) for adultery, as opposed to the unmarried person who is subject to flogging
key_terms.صَاغِر: Saghir: in a state of humiliation and subjugation, indicating the condemned is not given any honor

ai.seo_question: If a person being stoned for adultery flees from the pit, must they be returned to complete the punishment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (or al-Kadhim, peace be upon him) establishes a key juridical distinction in the law of stoning (rajm): if a person convicted by their own confession flees the pit after being struck by some stones, they are not to be returned, as their repentance through flight is implicitly honored. However, if convicted by witnesses while denying the charge, they must be returned humiliated. This ruling is grounded in the Prophetic precedent of Ma'iz ibn Malik, whose case the Prophet used to teach that those who confess are to be given the benefit of the doubt if they flee, and to highlight that Imam Ali's guidance would have prevented the error of killing Ma'iz after he fled.
